findings.text: non-blocking: the _READ_CONTEXT comment at reckon/run_store.py:929-930 and the stored_run_rows docstring at :1025 both claim 'a second thread or task decodes for itself', but a ContextVar set during a synchronous read is copied into every asyncio task created afterwards (asyncio.Task captures contextvars.copy_context() at creation; verified on this interpreter), so tasks created after a synchronous read share the parent's object and its cache, and only a fresh thread gets the default. The claim is false for tasks; the node's test at tests/test_an_unchanged_run_store_is_decoded_once.py:162 exercises only a threading.Thread, so a future async reader, or an async seam like the four paused-decoder guards, would not get the per-task isolation the comment promises.
